units:
Data Collection, Cleaning and 
Visualization

Learning Objectives
• Understand data collection methods
• Learn sources of data
• Understand data quality issues
• Learn basic visualization techniques
• Interpret visual data for decision making

What is Data Collection?
• Process of gathering and measuring 
information from various sources.
• Example: Collecting daily temperature data 
from weather stations.

Types of Data Collection
1. Primary Data
• Collected directly by researcher
• Surveys, experiments, observations
2. Secondary Data
• Already collected by others
• Government reports, databases

Primary Data Example – Survey
• Example: Student Satisfaction Survey
• Questions:
• Rate teaching quality (1–5)
• Rate infrastructure (1–5)
• Rate library facilities (1–5)
• Collected from 100 students.

Primary Data Example – Sensors
• Example: Smart Agriculture
Sensors collect:
• Soil moisture
• Temperature
• Humidity
• Used to optimize irrigation.

IOT devices in oil and chemical 
industries
• Pressure and Temperature Sensors: Monitor pressure and temperature levels in
pipelines, storage tanks, and processing equipment (Honeywell ST3000)
• Flow Meters: measure the rate of fluid movement in pipelines, especially
important in transporting oil, gas, and chemicals. (Siemens SITRANS FS230)
• Gas Leak Detectors: Identify the presence of hazardous gases, like methane, sulfur
dioxide, or hydrogen sulfide, in real-time. (MSA Altair 4X)
• Environmental and Emission Monitors: Monitor emissions from factories,
refineries, and other equipment, tracking pollutants to ensure regulatory
compliance. (Aeroqual Series 500, Thermo Fisher 42i NO-NO2-NOx Analyzer)
• Vibration Sensors (SKF CMSS 2200), Level Sensors (VEGA VEGAPULS 64), Wearable
IoT Devices for Safety, GPS Trackers and Fleet Management Devices etc.

Secondary Data Example
• Example: Using Government Open Data
• Dataset: City population data
• Year Population
• 2020 1,200,000
• 2021 1,260,000
• 2022 1,330,000

Data Collection Workflow
• Define problem
• Identify data sources
• Collect data
• Clean and validate data
• Store data
• Analyze and visualize

Data Quality Issues
• Common problems:
Missing values
Duplicate records
Incorrect measurements
Inconsistent formats
Example: Age recorded as 200 years.

Real World Case Study
• E-commerce company collects:
Customer purchases
Website clicks
Product ratings
• Visualizations used:
Sales trend graphs
Product popularity charts
Customer segmentation plots

Data Cleaning Techniques
• Handling Missing Values
• Removing Duplicate Data
• Handling Outliers (Z-score method, IQR (Interquartile Range), 
Visualization (box plot)
• Standardization / Normalization (Min-Max Normalization)
• Correcting Inconsistent Data
• Data Transformation
• Noise Reduction (Clustering)
• Data Integration Cleaning
• Data Validation (Ensure data follows rules.)
• Feature Encoding (Convert Categorical data into numerical)

Introduction to Data Visualization
• Data visualization converts data into graphical 
form.
• Purpose:
Understand patterns
Detect trends
Communicate insights

Common Visualization Types
• Bar Chart – compare categories
• Line Chart – show trends over time
• Pie Chart – show proportions
• Scatter Plot – show relationships

Bar Chart Example
• Student Enrollments
• Course Students
• AI 120
• Data Sci 90
• ML 110
• Cyber Sec 70
• Bar chart helps compare enrollments.

Line Chart Example
• Monthly Sales Data
• Jan 10k
• Feb 15k
• Mar 18k
• Apr 25k
• Line chart shows increasing trend.

Scatter Plot Example
• Study Hours vs Exam Score
• Hours Score
• 2 50
• 4 65
• 6 75
• 8 90
• Scatter plot shows positive relationship.

Summary
• Data collection is the first step in analytics
• Data can be primary or secondary
• Data must be cleaned before analysis
• Visualization helps understand patterns
• Used widely in business, science, and research
